problem_text:
A regional courier must dispatch a vehicle to service 11 distinct distribution hubs with the following geographical positions:

Hub Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (173,44)
Hub Beta: Positioned at grid reference (59,156)
Hub Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (76,156)
Hub Delta: Positioned at grid reference (22,180)
Hub Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (131,192)
Hub Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (72,197)
Hub Eta: Positioned at grid reference (90,105)
Hub Theta: Positioned at grid reference (117,13)
Hub Iota: Positioned at grid reference (161,178)
Hub Kappa: Positioned at grid reference (132,170)
Hub Lambda: Positioned at grid reference (166,140)

The travel distances between hubs, measured in kilometers, are precisely defined:

Iota to Lambda: 38.3 km

Due to a permanent infrastructure limitation, no direct roadway exists connecting Hub Alpha and Hub Beta.
Furthermore, owing to a scheduling and routing protocol, exactly one of the following two connections must be incorporated into the circuit: the link between Hub Beta and Hub Gamma, or the link between Hub Gamma and Hub Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-circuit route, where each hub is visited precisely once before returning to the origin, thereby minimizing the total travel distance.
